name: Wanderburg — Low-poly 3D (shipped)
description: THE presentation the game ships: a perspective camera over the rolling fortress, hand-built low-poly meshes, toon bands with environment ink edges, no silhouette outline (on convex hand-built meshes the inverted hull wins the depth tie and paints the object black), no shadow map — every hull drops its own blob shadow. Sun, sky and fog come from the biome (js/Content.js), so the variant pins only the shading model. Camera pose and the zoom range mirror Constants.js (CAMERA_*); the zoom itself stays authored by the game (CAMERA_ZOOM / CAMERA_ZOOM_MOBILE). Draw load, measured on a full valley (verify/deploy.mjs, C-6 revision): ~580-780 GL draws per frame (median over rendered frames, camera-dependent) at ~900 base + ~240 ink unique enabled mesh instances; the old \"4-8k draws/frame\" was an artifact of the CUMULATIVE device._drawCallsPerFrame counter (nothing resets it without profiling), and ink edges were not drawn at all until the engine fix of _inkEdgeMesh (GPU index buffers lock() to a raw ArrayBuffer; setPositions builds a PLANAR vertex buffer whose element stride is not fmt.size) — PlayArcEngine b813027. maxDrawCalls states the profile canon as PER-FRAME GL draws (900; measured 762 with the ink on); WORLD3D_TOON_INK=1 (actors only) or 0 is the mobile lever on the instance census. Every entity is SELF-PRESENTED (GAME_SPEC.entities declare representation "none"): js/WanderView.js + js/WanderMesh.js build the meshes on the kit engine layer, so the pipeline binds no second copy of anything.
